newsitem.title: USA: Excel pork unit chief to step down,successor named.
newsitem.headline: Excel pork unit chief to step down,successor named.

text.p: Lee Worth, general manager of North American pork operations for Excel Corp., a division of privately held Cargill Inc, and president of Cargill's worldwide pork operations will retire at the end of the month, a Cargill spokeswoman said.
"Lee has decided to take early retirement effective May 31," said Linda Thrane, manager of Cargill public relations.
Gary Kohake, 44, senior vice president for North American pork operations will assume Worth's duties, said Greg Lauser, another Cargill spokesman.
Excel, one of the top meat processors in the country, operates pork plants in Ottumwa, Iowa, Marshall, Mo., and Beardstown, Ill.
Thrane said Worth announced his decision on Wednesday.

Worth, 57, joined Cargill's meat sector as vice president in 1991 after leaving Farmstead Foods Inc. of Albert Lea, Minn. as president and chief executive officer, Lauser said. Worth was appointed general manager of North American pork operations in 1992 and president of Cargill's worldwide pork operations in 1994, Lauser said.
